- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction, especially after sharp spikes.
- After a price spike (e.g., >83), model often overshoots and fails to correct — reduce forecast slope in next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to counteract mean reversion bias.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias in 30-day horizon — if forecast is >82.5, reduce by 0.5–1.5% per day until price stabilizes.
- When sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33 → 0.67), model misreads momentum — use weighted average of recent 5-day sentiment to adjust forecast direction.
- If true outcome drops below 70 after 10+ days of high prices, model often fails to recognize structural correction — apply early warning bias: reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 3 days.
